Grasshoppers sit near a hundred-gram portion, with less protein than beef but far less fat; crickets are paired with calcium, and termites and caterpillars with iron.

pages.text: Crickets or Cows? Eating insects is also good for the planet. To feed a growing human population, global farming has to expand. Yet farming for billions of people greatly harms the planet. One cause of this is a demand for beef. Raising cows hurts the planet in several ways. Cows give off a greenhouse gas that helps cause global warming. A cattle ranch ten times more than a large insect farm. Also, insect waste is a and good for the soil.
pages.brief: A cattle ranch stretches beside a much smaller insect farm, making clear the difference in land use. Cows graze and give off greenhouse gas linked to global warming, while insect trays sit in a compact farm. Insect waste is shown enriching soil in a garden.

pages.text: Much of the world’s farmland is used to raise and feed cows. Insect farms take up far less space. They also need much less food to provide the same amount of nutrients. Most cows today eat grain, which needs large amounts of land and water to grow. In some parts of the world, farmers clear more trees each year to make room for cattle. This destroys homes for thousands of species already at risk. The best way to save these forests may be to offer people insect protein.
pages.brief: A wide farmland area grows grain for cows, while a much smaller insect farm takes up far less space. In another area, farmers clear trees for cattle pasture, removing homes for wildlife. Nearby, people look at insect protein as a way to save forests.

pages.text: Popular Bugs and Ways to Eat Them There are more than 2,000 edible insects around the world. People eat them in all sorts of ways. In Thailand, some outdoor stands sell crispy, fried water bugs. People add sauce just as others might put mustard or ketchup on a hot dog. Other people snack on grasshoppers and bamboo worms.
pages.brief: A busy outdoor market in Thailand has stands selling crispy, fried water bugs. A vendor serves a tray of water bugs, and a customer adds sauce the way someone might put mustard or ketchup on a hot dog. Nearby, people snack on grasshoppers and bamboo worms.

pages.text: Sushi and Snails Food culture changes. There was a time when Italians thought tomatoes were poisonous. Americans once disliked lobster and fed it to prisoners. Few cultures ate raw fish fifty years ago. Now sushi is popular all over the globe. In French restaurants, snails are a popular appetizer. The dish is called escargot (es-car-GO), the French word for “snail.” The snails are taken out of their shells, cooked, and placed back inside the shells. Diners use special tools to pull out the snail meat. Water bugs boiled in a special sauce can be found in some restaurants in China. The bugs and sauce are served over rice. When the weather gets chilly, some people have a steaming bowl of ant soup.
pages.brief: A French restaurant diner uses a special tool to pull snail meat from a shell. Nearby, a Chinese restaurant serves water bugs boiled in sauce over rice, and someone holds a steaming bowl of ant soup in chilly weather. A plate of sushi and a lobster show foods people once avoided.

pages.text: One town in Brazil cooks queen ants every October and November. This is when queen ants come out from hiding underground. People collect the ants and remove their wings. Some fry the ants. Others dip them in chocolate. The people say queen ants have a minty taste. Edible Arthropods Most arthropod species are insects. Lobsters, crabs, spiders, scorpions, and many other animals are also arthropods. These animals all have their skeletons on the outside of their bodies. The tasty meat is on the inside. Some outer shells can be eaten, too.
pages.brief: In a Brazilian town, people collect queen ants emerging from underground, remove the wings, and fry some while dipping others in chocolate. Nearby, a display of arthropods: lobster, crab, spider, scorpion and insects, shows their outside skeletons, with edible meat inside and some edible shells.

pages.text: In Mexico, some people enjoy French-fried caterpillars or ant eggs covered in butter. For dessert, chocolate-covered locusts or candy-covered worms are sweet treats. Central Africa has a wide range of edible insects. In Ghana, many people fry or roast termites. They can also be ground into flour for baking.
pages.brief: In Mexico, a plate holds French-fried caterpillars and ant eggs covered in butter, while chocolate-covered locusts and candy-covered worms are set out for dessert. In Ghana, people fry and roast termites, then grind some into flour for baking, showing Central Africa's wide range of edible insects.

pages.text: Some Australians munch on witchetty grubs, which look like large white caterpillars. These insects have crisp skin and a smooth filling that tastes like nuts. Some restaurants in Japan serve fried silk moth cocoons. Fried grasshoppers and other insects are sold in some stores.
pages.brief: An Australian outdoors scene shows people eating witchetty grubs that look like large white caterpillars, with crisp skin and a smooth, nutty filling. In Japan, a restaurant serves fried silk moth cocoons, and a store displays fried grasshoppers and other insects for sale.

pages.text: Be Careful! Never eat wild insects! It’s very important to remember that. Walking into your backyard for a buggy snack can be dangerous. Insects that live outside can be covered with stuff that might harm you if you eat it. Also, some insects are poisonous and can make you very sick.
pages.brief: A child looks at an insect in a backyard and does not eat it; the scene shows why wild insects should never be eaten. Outside insects can be covered with something harmful, and some are poisonous and can make a person very sick. Wild bugs are not a safe snack.

pages.text: People who cook and eat insects should be careful to buy them from farms. Farmed insects have special diets. They don’t contain things that might harm people. In the United States, the best way to find edible insects is on the Internet. People can find live insects, meals made with insects, and tasty insect recipes.
pages.brief: At a farm, workers tend insects kept on special diets, and a cook buys farmed insects instead of wild ones. A person in the United States uses a computer to find live insects, insect meals, and tasty insect recipes online, showing a safer way to get edible insects.

pages.text: Let’s Start Cooking! David George Gordon, a chef from Washington, wrote the Eat-A-Bug Cookbook. People like his pasta with six-legged meatballs, which are made with crickets. Other favorites are fried tarantula and white chocolate and waxworm cookies. Gordon believes that eating insects is a better way to get protein than eating chicken, cows, or pigs. Insects are cheap and easy to farm in plain fish tanks. Raising them does not harm the planet. Insects may just be the food of the future.
pages.brief: Chef David George Gordon stands in a kitchen with pasta and six-legged meatballs made from crickets, fried tarantula, and white chocolate and waxworm cookies. He compares insect protein with chicken, cows and pigs, and shows insects farmed cheaply in plain fish tanks as a planet-friendly food of the future.

books.title: The Force of Water
books.art_why: The book explains real rivers, landforms, floods and water use that can be photographed today.

pages.text: In The Force of Water readers will learn about how water changes our planet’s surface, how it changes form as it moves through the water cycle, and why it’s so important to living things. A map and graphs support comprehension.
pages.brief: A wide river rushing over rocks in a green valley, white water churning as it flows downstream, with the far bank and wooded hills behind it. The scene shows the powerful movement of water across the land in full daylight.

pages.text: Introduction Water, Earth’s most important resource, is a mighty force. It covers most of Earth and is always at work changing Earth’s surface. Plants, animals, and humans need water to survive. So, we have to take care of the water for the good of the Earth.
pages.brief: A broad view of Earth's surface where water is at work: a river winding through a valley, a lake, and a coastline meeting the sea. Land, plants and animals all appear together near the water in bright natural light.

pages.text: Water is found above ground in lakes, ponds, rivers, streams, and oceans. It is also found below ground, between rocks and sand. This water is called groundwater. The air also holds water as clouds and an invisible gas called water vapor.
pages.brief: A split view of where water hides: a lake and a stream above the ground, rocks and wet sand with groundwater between them below, and puffy clouds drifting in the sky above the landscape.

pages.text: Water on the Move Much of Earth’s water is on the move. Water falls from clouds as rain and snow and drains into streams and rivers. The land surrounding streams and rivers is called a watershed. Streams flow into small rivers, and small rivers flow into bigger rivers. The smaller streams and rivers that flow into bigger rivers are called tributaries. Over time, much of the water that flows into streams and rivers reaches the oceans.
pages.brief: Rain and snow falling from dark clouds onto a hillside, water draining into small streams that join into a widening river. The surrounding land that sheds water into the streams is shown spreading out around them.

pages.text: M i s s i s M i s o u R R e r i v R O UNITED STATES M R i v e GULF OF MEXICO.
pages.brief: An aerial view of a huge river system winding south across open land, many smaller channels joining the main river until it spreads into a wide gulf. Green fields and forests cover the land on both sides.

pages.text: Water as a Force As water flows in rivers and streams, it picks up dirt, sand, and rocks. The dirt and sand carried by water are called sediment. Sediment helps water carve away the land. The Grand Canyon is one of Earth’s largest canyons. Over millions of years, it was carved by the fast-moving Colorado River. It shows how powerful water can be.
pages.brief: The Colorado River cutting through the deep layered walls of the Grand Canyon, sunlight and shadow on the rock. Brown water carries sand and small stones downstream, showing how moving water carves away the land over time.

pages.text: When water slows down, the sediment settles to the bottom of the stream or river. Deposits of sediment form new land, called sandbars and deltas. Large deltas form where big rivers meet oceans.
pages.brief: A slow, wide river spreading out at its mouth into a fan of new sandy land where it meets the ocean, with sandbars of pale sediment sitting in the shallows and muddy banks along the quiet water.

pages.text: Flooding Sometimes massive amounts of rain and snow fall to Earth, causing streams and rivers to spill over their banks. The land around the streams and rivers floods when this happens. Flooding can cause lots of damage.
pages.brief: Muddy floodwater spilling over the banks of a swollen river and covering low fields and roads, with trees standing in the water. The surrounding land is submerged after heavy rain fell across the region.

pages.text: When the water recedes to the riverbed, the dirt carried by the floodwater is left on land. Over the years, this dirt forms a floodplain. The soil of a floodplain is rich in nutrients from the river. Crops grow well in floodplains, but can be ruined when water floods the area again.
pages.brief: A river back in its channel after a flood, dark rich soil left spread across the flat land on either side. Green crops grow in neat rows on the fertile ground beside the water.

pages.text: Water Is Important Rivers and streams have many uses besides carving land. People use rivers for swimming, boating, and fishing. People also have used rivers for thousands of years to transport goods from place to place. Today, large barges and ships move cargo over rivers. Lumber logs from forests to mills over rivers.
pages.brief: People swimming, boating and fishing on a wide river while a large barge loaded with cargo moves along it and cut logs float downstream toward a mill on the bank.

pages.text: Dams built on rivers use the force of water to make electricity. Factories use millions of gallons of water each year to make the things people use. Farms to irrigate crops. We use water in our homes to clean and cook. How else do you use water in your home?
pages.brief: A dam holding back a river with water rushing through its turbines, and nearby a factory, a farm with irrigated crop rows, and a home kitchen where water runs from a tap for cleaning and cooking.

pages.text: Streams and rivers are home to many living things. People and other animals depend on streams and rivers for drinking water. Some industries and large cities dump their waste into rivers, and this waste pollutes the water. Polluted water is harmful to humans, plants, and other animals that live in the water or use it to stay alive.
pages.brief: A clear stream full of life, with small fish and water plants and animals drinking at the edge, beside a pipe emptying dirty waste into a river where the water turns cloudy and polluted.

pages.text: The World’s Rivers Nile, North Africa 6,677 km (4,150 mi) Amazon, South America 6,280 km (3,900 mi) Yangtze, China 6,115 km (3,800 mi) Mississippi, United States 3,780 km (2,350 mi) Volga, Russia 3,740 km (2,325 mi) Mackenzie, Canada 1,802 km (1,120 mi) River Dee, UK 110 km (70 mi) Conclusion The force of water running in rivers and streams changes the shape of the land in many ways. Rivers and streams are important to humans, other animals, and plants. Rivers and streams will take care of us as long as we take care of them.
pages.brief: Several great rivers of the world shown flowing through different landscapes: a desert river in North Africa, a rainforest river in South America, a river in China, a wide North American river, and northern rivers among forests and hills.

books.title: China
books.art_why: China is a real country that exists today, so photographs are the right choice; it is not about a named famous person.

pages.text: China Where Is It? The People’s Republic of China is one of the largest countries in the world, along with Russia, Canada, and the United States. Russia and China cover a large part of the continent of Asia. In fact, China is almost as large as the entire continent of Europe. Many countries border China, including India, Mongolia, Russia, and North Korea. To the east of China are the Pacific Ocean, the South China Sea, and the East China Sea. China has about 14,500 kilometers (9,000 mi.) of coastline.
pages.brief: A wide, high view of the continent of Asia, with China stretching across a huge part of it beside Russia, and the faraway lands of Canada and the United States for comparison. India, Mongolia, Russia and North Korea lie along China's borders, and the Pacific Ocean, South China Sea and East China Sea meet its long eastern coastline.

pages.text: The Forbidden City in Beijing was built in the early 1400s. It first housed the emperor’s family in 1420. China has several large cities, including Shanghai, Beijing, and Hong Kong. Beijing, the capital, is located in northeast China. Its name has changed many times, yet Beijing is one of the oldest cities in the world. It is over three thousand years old. More than fifteen million people live there today. Beijing is a mixture of both ancient and modern buildings. Skyscrapers reach for the sky beside buildings that have stood for hundreds of years. At the center of Beijing is the Forbidden City. This palace was built in the fifteenth century. It was the home of China’s emperors for more than five hundred years. It is called the Forbidden City because only the emperor of China could enter every area in it. Today, the palace is a museum.
pages.brief: The Forbidden City in Beijing, a vast palace of red walls and golden roofs at the centre of the city, open today as a museum. Around it modern skyscrapers rise beside buildings hundreds of years old, and more than fifteen million people fill the streets of this ancient capital in northeast China.

pages.text: People More than 1.3 billion people live in China. That is more people than in any other country. The United States has about 316 million people. That’s about one quarter the size of China’s population. A village in China More than half of the people in China live in towns, villages, or the countryside. People who live in rural regions often grow crops and raise livestock for food. Meanwhile, people who live in towns and villages may manufacture goods as well as perform other jobs. Many people also live in large cities, which are centers for trade and business. Many different ethnic groups live in China. The Han is the largest group. Other groups include the Hui (HWAY), Zhuang (JWAHNG), Dai (DY), Yao (YOW), Miao (MEOW), Tibetans (teh-BET-uhns), Manchus (MAN-chooz), and Mongolians (mahn-GOH-lee-uhns). Most Chinese people speak Mandarin, which means “common language.” People in China also speak many other languages, including Cantonese and English.
pages.brief: A Chinese village in the countryside, where farmers tend crops and raise livestock for food. Nearby, people in a town make goods in workshops, while a busy city behind them is full of trade and business. Han, Hui, Zhuang, Dai, Yao, Miao, Tibetan, Manchu and Mongolian people speak Mandarin and many other languages.

pages.text: Mandarin Characters Here are the Mandarin characters for some words. It can take years to master the art of calligraphy. Every line or dot must be perfectly spaced, showing balance and beauty. Chinese writing does not use the letters of the English alphabet. Instead, it uses thousands of characters that stand for words or parts of words. Some of these characters look like what they mean. For example, the character for the word forest looks like three trees in a forest. Chinese artists have been creating amazing works for thousands of years. One of the more interesting art forms is calligraphy, which is a combination of art and writing. Calligraphers use ink to create beautiful Chinese characters. The characters combine to create stunning images as well as powerful poetry.
pages.brief: A calligrapher's hand holding a brush dipped in ink, drawing careful lines and dots on paper, each one perfectly spaced so the character looks balanced and beautiful. Beside it, the character for forest looks like three trees standing together, one of thousands of characters that stand for words instead of letters.

pages.text: China’s Landforms Land Because China is so large, it has many different landforms. Deserts, mountains, and canyons stretch across the northwest region. This area also includes one of the lowest places on Earth. It is a salt lake located in the Turfan Depression. The lake is 154 meters (505 ft.) below sea level. In the southwest, several mountain ranges reach up into the sky. The most famous range is the Himalayas. This range includes the highest mountain in the world, Mount Everest. The southwest also includes high plateaus.
pages.brief: Deserts, mountains and deep canyons stretch across northwest China, and a salt lake lies 154 metres below sea level in the Turfan Depression. In the southwest the Himalaya mountain ranges reach into the sky, with the snow-covered peak of Mount Everest, the highest mountain in the world, rising above high plateaus.

pages.text: Tian Shan (tsee-EN SHAHN) Mountains Bamboo forest Yellow River In the east, the land includes flat plains, wetlands, and forests. This flat land is the only land suited to farming. Part of the Yangtze (yank-SEE) River flows through this region, as well as part of the Yellow River. These rivers help provide water for the fields. Farmers grow rice, wheat, potatoes, and peanuts. Other crops include tea, barley, and cotton. In addition, many people across China raise animals, such as chickens, goats, pigs, sheep, and cattle.
pages.brief: Flat plains, wetlands and forests in eastern China, the only land suited to farming. The Yangtze and Yellow rivers flow through the fields, where farmers grow rice, wheat, potatoes, peanuts, tea, barley and cotton, and keep chickens, goats, pigs, sheep and cattle. Behind them rise the Tian Shan mountains and a stand of bamboo forest.

pages.text: History Experts estimate that Chinese civilization began over five thousand years ago! In fact, some of the oldest artifacts in the world have been found in China. Ancient Chinese people kept good records, which have helped experts learn about the country’s history. The ancient Chinese named their land Zhongguo (JOONG-gwah), which means “the Middle Kingdom.” They believed that it was the center of the civilized world. In order to protect the land from invaders from Mongolia, the Chinese emperor began building a giant wall. Work began around 220 bc and continued for nearly 2,000 years. The Great Wall is actually a series of walls in northern China and southern Mongolia. One of the sections stretches for about 8,850 kilometers (5,500 mi.). For more than three thousand years, parts of China were ruled by emperors. Sometimes one family would rule an area for hundreds of years. This was known as a dynasty. Under these dynasties, China became an advanced civilization. Great Wall of China.
pages.brief: Ancient Chinese artefacts and careful written records, and the Great Wall under construction: workers building the giant wall across northern China and southern Mongolia to keep out invaders, a task that went on for nearly two thousand years. The wall stretches for about 8,850 kilometres, the work of emperors and their dynasties.

pages.text: Confucius Kong Fuzi (KOHNG FOO-tsu), also known as Confucius (kuhn-FYOO- shuhs), was a Chinese philosopher and teacher. Confucius believed that people, including government leaders, should serve others. He also believed that all people had the right to an education. Confucius died in 479 bc, but his teachings are still followed today. The ancient Chinese people discovered and invented many things we still use today. They were the first to create paper, nearly two thousand years ago. They also invented the magnetic compass, which helped sailors find their way. Gunpowder is another Chinese invention. They used it to blast rocks apart and make fireworks for celebrations. The ancient Chinese were also the first to make fabric from silk. It became the country’s most popular export for many years. People traveled from around the world on a trade route called the Silk Road to get it. The fibers used to make silk come from the cocoons of silkworms. The ancient Chinese discovered they could separate the fibers from the cocoon. Then, they spun the fibers together to make a strong thread. The thread was woven together to make beautiful cloth.
pages.brief: The philosopher and teacher Confucius, standing before pupils he believed should all have the right to an education. Around him are Chinese inventions: sheets of paper, a magnetic compass for sailors, gunpowder blasting rock and lighting fireworks, and silk cloth unwound from silkworm cocoons and carried along the Silk Road trade route.

pages.text: The Chinese New Year celebration lasts two weeks and includes dances such as this fire dragon dance. Celebrations One of the most widely celebrated holidays in China is the New Year. The Chinese New Year takes place in late January or early February, depending on the Chinese calendar. During the festival, dancers carry colorful dragons or lions through the streets. People light firecrackers and enjoy feasts. They decorate their doorways with poetry written on strips of red paper. These traditions are thought to bring good luck in the coming year. The Lantern Festival is another popular celebration in China. Held soon after the Chinese New Year, it celebrates the first full moon of the year. People hang colorful paper lanterns outside with riddles attached. Others try to solve the riddles to receive a small gift. People also enjoy sweet dumplings made of rice flour.
pages.brief: Dancers carrying a colourful fire dragon through a street at Chinese New Year, firecrackers popping overhead and families sharing feasts. Doorways are decorated with poetry on strips of red paper. Later, at the Lantern Festival, colourful paper lanterns with riddles hang outside and people eat sweet dumplings made of rice flour.

pages.text: Dumplings are popular in many areas of China. They are filled with meat or vegetables. Food Rice is the basis for many meals in China. Other common ingredients are noodles, potatoes, meat, fish, and tofu. The typical meals can be different depending on the region. In some parts of China, the food may be very spicy. In the southeast near the ocean, seafood is a main part of many dishes. In the north, many people use wheat instead of rice. For dessert, many Chinese people have seasonal fruit. They may also enjoy candies, pancakes, or a dish made of shaved ice and fruit called baobing (BOU-beeng).
pages.brief: A table of Chinese food: bowls of rice and noodles, potatoes, meat, fish and tofu, spicy dishes, and seafood from the southeast, with wheat breads in the north. Beside them sit dumplings filled with meat or vegetables, a bowl of baobing, shaved ice with fruit, and seasonal fruit for dessert.

pages.text: Every year, millions of people visit the Great Wall of China. It is considered by many Chinese people to be the country’s national symbol. Conclusion China’s history stretches back thousands of years. Its diverse people have created interesting and unique cultures. Stretching across much of Asia, its wonders include breathtaking mountains, the Great Wall, delicious food, and exciting celebrations. If you visited China, which wonder would you want to experience first?
pages.brief: Millions of visitors walk along the Great Wall of China, the country's national symbol, winding over green hills. Beyond it stretch breathtaking mountains, and below lie the delicious foods and exciting celebrations of China's diverse people, whose history reaches back thousands of years.

pages.text: China Population: 1,355,692,576 Land: 9,569,901 sq km (3,694,959 sq. mi.) Capital City: Beijing Primary Language: Mandarin Primary Religions: Daoism, Buddhism Currency: Yuan (yoo-WAHN)
pages.brief: A view of China today: the crowded streets of Beijing, the capital, where people speak Mandarin; the temples of Daoism and Buddhism; and Yuan notes and coins, the country's currency, beside the wide land that holds more than 1.3 billion people.

books.title: India
books.art_why: India, its people, cities, landmarks, landforms, and wildlife all exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: India offers readers a well-rounded overview of many aspects of this country.
pages.brief: A title-page image for a book about India, offering a broad overview of the country. Small scenes suggest the book’s main aspects: location, people, land, celebrations, history, and animals, with a calm, inviting composition that introduces India as a country with many aspects to discover.

pages.text: India China India ASIA Where Is It? India is a country in Asia that is mainly a peninsula. Along the northern edge of India are the countries of Pakistan, China, Nepal (nuh-PAHL), and Bhutan (boo-TAHN). To the east are Bangladesh (bahng-gluh-DESH) and Myanmar (mee-AHN-mar). Just south of India is the island of Sri Lanka (SHREE LAHNG- kuh). To the southwest of India is the Arabian Sea. To the southeast is the Bay of Bengal. India also includes some groups of islands.
pages.brief: A geographic view of Asia centered on India as a peninsula. Pakistan, China, Nepal, and Bhutan lie along the north; Bangladesh and Myanmar are to the east; Sri Lanka is south. The Arabian Sea lies southwest, the Bay of Bengal southeast, and small island groups are included.

pages.text: The capital of India is New Delhi (DEL-ee), which is part of the larger city of Delhi. The two areas are very different. Delhi is a very old city, but New Delhi was built in the 1920s and 1930s. Delhi is a complex maze of small streets crowded with small shops, while New Delhi has wide streets and modern shopping centers. More than twenty million people live in Delhi and New Delhi combined.
pages.brief: A split city view of Delhi and New Delhi. Old Delhi is a dense maze of narrow streets crowded with small shops and people. New Delhi has wide streets and modern shopping centers, showing the contrast between the old city and the newer capital area, home to more than twenty million people combined.

pages.text: People More than one billion people live in India. Only China has more people. Most Indian people live in the countryside, even though India does have some large cities. Most homes in the rural areas don’t have running water. People must go to a well and bring home water every day. About half of the people in rural areas don’t have electricity, either. Half of the people in India make their living growing crops, mainly grains. They also raise cattle, water buffalo, and other animals. However, most Indian people do not raise cattle to eat, because many religions in India, including Hinduism, believe cows are sacred. They use cattle for plowing their fields and for transportation. They raise sheep, goats, and chickens for meat. The Taj Mahal The Taj Mahal (TAHZH muh- HAHL) is one of the most well-known landmarks in India. It was built by the emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal after she died. It took forced laborers twenty-two years to complete the Taj Mahal.
pages.brief: A rural Indian village where people carry water from a well because homes lack running water, and farmers plow fields with cattle while water buffalo, sheep, goats, and chickens are nearby. In the background, the Taj Mahal appears as a grand white landmark built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal.

pages.text: Most Indian cities are extremely crowded. Many people live in apartment buildings along very narrow streets. Because India has such a large population, it has been hard for the country’s electricity supply to keep up with the demand. In some Indian cities, it’s very common for the power to go out. The center of Hindi language filmmaking is Mumbai (mum-BY). It was once known as Bombay because the British pronounced Mumbai incorrectly. Mumbai releases more than a thousand movies per year. It is called Bollywood locally and globally. The Bollywood audience is global, as well.
pages.brief: A crowded Indian city with apartment buildings along narrow streets and many people. A power outage dims some buildings, showing strain on electricity. In Mumbai, a busy film studio suggests Bollywood filmmaking, with cameras and sets reflecting the release of more than a thousand movies a year for a global audience.

pages.text: India’s Landforms India Land The Himalayas (him-uh-LAY-uhz) form India’s northern border. They are the highest mountains in the world and cut off India from the rest of Asia. This is why India is sometimes called a subcontinent. A low-lying plain stretches across northern India. This rich land was formed long ago as rivers flooded and left soil behind. The Thar Desert is in western India.
pages.brief: A wide landform view of India: the towering Himalayas along the northern border, a low-lying fertile plain stretching across the north, and the dry Thar Desert in the west. The mountains rise high and separate India from the rest of Asia.

pages.text: The Ganges (GAN-jeez) and Indus Rivers lie in the northern plains of India. For Hindus, the Ganges is a sacred river. Hindus from all over India travel to the river to enter its waters. South of the Indus and Ganges Rivers lies raised land that takes up more than half of India. In May or June every year, winds bring rain as they blow northward from the Indian Ocean. This is the monsoon season. During this time, rain falls almost every day in the afternoon. Most of India’s rain falls during this hot, wet season.
pages.brief: The Ganges and Indus Rivers flow across northern India. Hindus gather at the sacred Ganges to enter its waters. South of the rivers lies raised land, while monsoon winds from the Indian Ocean bring heavy afternoon rains across India during the hot, wet season.

pages.text: Celebrations People in India celebrate many special days. Diwali (dee-VAH-lee) is a festival that lasts for five days. During this time, people across religions light small candles. They shoot firecrackers and give sweets and other gifts to friends and family. Holi (HOH-lee) is a spring Hindu celebration known as the festival of colors. Today, people of all religions celebrate Holi to mark the end of winter. They throw colored water and powder on each other. Children use water guns filled with colored water to spray colors on their friends. People also sing, dance, and enjoy special foods and drinks.
pages.brief: A celebration scene showing Diwali with small candles, firecrackers, sweets, and gifts shared among friends and family. Nearby, Holi celebrants throw colored water and powder, and children spray colored water with water guns. People sing, dance, and enjoy special foods and drinks to mark the end of winter.

pages.text: History India’s civilization is very old. About 2,300 years ago, people living in the land now known as India had been mostly united under one ruler. About 1,300 years ago Muslims set up a kingdom with Delhi at its center. Muslim rule lasted until the 1600s. Europeans had landed in India as early as 1498. That’s when Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama (VAHS-koh DAH GAH-mah) sailed to India. By 1858, Great Britain had taken control of the country. In the 1920s, a lawyer named Mohandas Gandhi (moh-huhn- DAHS GAHN-dee) joined the movement to resist British rule. He asked them to protest British rule in nonviolent, or peaceful, ways. By 1947, India was free. Since gaining independence, India has faced many obstacles but continues to grow. India elected its first woman prime minister, Indira Gandhi, in 1966. Forty-one years later, in 2007, it elected its first woman president.
pages.brief: A history montage of India: an ancient ruler’s united land, a Delhi-centered Muslim kingdom, Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama arriving by ship in 1498, and British rule by 1858. Mohandas Gandhi leads peaceful resistance, India becomes free in 1947, and later Indira Gandhi and a woman president appear.

pages.text: Animals India’s wildlife includes many exciting species. India is the only country in the world with both lions and tigers. It is also the home of two kinds of leopards. The snow leopard of the Himalayas is very rare. One of India’s most famous reptiles is the cobra. The Indian cobra hunts small animals, such as rats and mice. It has been known to bite humans because its prey often lives in towns and villages.
pages.brief: A wildlife scene in India showing lions and tigers together, two kinds of leopards, and a rare snow leopard in the Himalayas. At the edge of a town or village, an Indian cobra hunts rats and mice, a reminder that its prey often lives near people.

pages.text: The Indian elephant is very strong. People once used it to lift logs in India’s forests. They also used it to carry crops and people. Some people still use the elephant to help them with their work. Today, wild Indian elephants are found in most parts of India. They are endangered, though, because of the loss of their habitat. Near the Bay of Bengal, the mangrove forests provide a special habitat for sea turtles, sharks, and crocodiles. This saltwater swamp is also the largest home of Bengal tigers in the world. A male Bengal tiger can grow to 3 meters (10 ft.) in length. It can weigh as much as 230 kilograms (500 lbs.). The tigers often swim in the swamp waters to catch prey.
pages.brief: An Indian elephant lifts logs and carries crops or people in a forest, while wild elephants roam nearby. Near the Bay of Bengal, mangrove swamp waters hold sea turtles, sharks, crocodiles, and Bengal tigers; a large male tiger swims through the swamp to catch prey.

pages.text: Conclusion India has a long history. It also has a very large, diverse population. It’s a country trying to find a balance between caring for its people and maintaining its natural beauty. Fascinating animals and interesting people make India a unique country with much to learn about.
pages.brief: A concluding overview of India: a country with a long history and a large, diverse population, trying to balance the needs of its people with care for its natural beauty. Fascinating animals and interesting people appear together, suggesting India is a unique country with much to learn.

pages.text: India Population: 1.4 billion Land: 2,973,193 sq km (1,147,956 sq. mi.) Capital City: New Delhi Primary Language: Hindi Primary Religion: Hinduism Currency: Rupee (ROO-pee)
pages.brief: A broad overview of India with a very large population, New Delhi as the capital city, Hindi as the primary language, Hinduism as the primary religion, and the rupee as the currency. The land covers about 2,973,193 square kilometers, or 1,147,956 square miles.

books.title: Incredible Places to Stay
books.art_why: Real hotels, animals, and places can be photographed.

pages.text: Places to Stay Places to Stay Have you ever visited a hotel made out of ice? How about a hotel located underwater? Incredible Places to Stay explores these and many other fascinating hotels around the world. Photographs of these unique places help further engage students with this interesting topic.
pages.brief: An ice hotel room with carved frozen walls and a bed, beside an underwater hotel room surrounded by blue water. These two extraordinary places welcome travelers who want an unusual night’s stay, hinting at many more fascinating hotels around the world.

pages.text: World Map of Incredible Hotels 2 1 1 5 2 6 3 7 4 8 Introduction Get ready to go on a tour of some of the world’s most unusual and amazing hotels. You’ll spend nights on four continents. You’ll swim to the bottom of the sea, sleep in a cave, and meet endangered animals. As different as these hotels are, they all share one thing: each offers you an incredible experience. Pack your bags and let’s go!
pages.brief: A broad world view suggests a tour across four continents, with distant hotel locations and unusual stays. Scenes hint at nights under the sea, inside a cave, and near endangered animals, inviting travelers to pack their bags for an incredible journey.

pages.text: Sky High The first stop on your tour is Skylodge Adventure Suites in the Sacred Valley of Cuzco, Peru. Getting to Skylodge is not easy! You will need to hike up a mountain or ride zip lines just to get to your room. Once you reach the top, you can sleep in a see-through capsule hanging high above the valley floor. Each capsule is solar powered and has a 300-degree view of Sacred Valley. You will eat dinner and breakfast in a see-through capsule, too, and you can watch the birds above you. You’ll feel just like you’re in a giant bird nest!
pages.brief: High on a mountain in Peru’s Sacred Valley, hikers and zip-line riders reach Skylodge Adventure Suites. A transparent capsule hangs above the valley floor with a wide view; inside, visitors eat dinner and breakfast and watch birds flying overhead, feeling as if they are in a giant bird nest.

pages.text: A Cool Place to Stay From Cuzco, you’ll travel to the Hôtel de Glace (O-tel DEH GLAHS). It is a cool hotel located just a few minutes outside of Quebec City, Canada. How cool is it? It’s a work of art made of ice! The rooms, halls, and most of the furniture are carved out of ice. Artists and workers spend about forty days every winter building the hotel because it all melts away in warm weather.
pages.brief: Outside Quebec City, Canada, artists and workers build the Hôtel de Glace from ice. Carved rooms, halls, and furniture gleam inside the frozen hotel, which takes about forty days each winter to create and melts away when warm weather returns.

pages.text: You’ll need to wear your heavy winter clothes during your stay. The temperature in the hotel is only 23° to 27°F (–5° to –3°C). It’s as cold as a freezer in there! You’ll sleep in a special extra-warm sleeping bag because the beds are made out of thick slabs of ice.
pages.brief: Inside the ice hotel, a guest wears heavy winter clothes in a freezing room. The temperature is as cold as a freezer, and the bed is made from thick slabs of ice, covered with a special extra-warm sleeping bag for the night.

pages.text: Breakfast with Giraffes The next stop on your tour is Nairobi, Kenya. There, at Giraffe Manor, you will share breakfast with some very special guests. The forests around Giraffe Manor are home to Rothschild’s giraffes. These giraffes are some of the tallest in the world. Adults can measure up to 20 feet (6 m) from their hooves to the tops of their heads.
pages.brief: At Giraffe Manor in Nairobi, Kenya, guests prepare to share breakfast with special guests. In the forests around the hotel live Rothschild’s giraffes, some of the tallest in the world, with adults measuring up to twenty feet from hooves to head tops.

pages.text: Every morning, the giraffes leave the forest and visit the hotel. They stick their heads through open windows and doors. Guests feed them pellets made from dry grass, corn, and molasses. Giraffe Manor is more than a nice hotel. Profits from the hotel go to a local wildlife conservation center.
pages.brief: Every morning at Giraffe Manor, giraffes leave the forest and visit the hotel, sticking their heads through open windows and doors. Guests feed them pellets made from dry grass, corn, and molasses; profits from the hotel support a local wildlife conservation center.

pages.text: In the Trees From Kenya, you’ll travel to Harads, in northern Sweden. There you’ll find the Treehotel—a hotel made up of strange tree houses. During your visit, you will stay in one of six separate tree-house rooms. The rooms hang 14 to 20 feet (4 to 6 m) off the ground. Each of the tree-house rooms is unique, but three of them are extra special. The outside of one of these rooms, the Mirrorcube, is covered with glass that reflects the woods around it. The glass makes the room nearly invisible.
pages.brief: In Harads, northern Sweden, the Treehotel offers six separate tree-house rooms hanging fourteen to twenty feet above the ground. One extra-special room, the Mirrorcube, is covered with glass that reflects the surrounding woods, making it nearly invisible among the trees.

pages.text: The Bird’s Nest tree house is completely covered in a tangle of tree branches. It looks like the home of an enormous bird. The UFO is a strange room built to look like a flying saucer. The UFO has outside landing lights and a ladder that you can bring inside at night. It looks as though an alien has come to Earth for a vacation.
pages.brief: At the Treehotel, the Bird’s Nest tree house is covered in a tangle of branches and looks like an enormous bird’s home. Nearby, the UFO room resembles a flying saucer, with outside landing lights and a ladder that can be pulled inside at night.

pages.text: A Room Without a View While you’re in Sweden, you can stop in the town of Sala. There you’ll find the deepest hotel room in the world. The Sala Silvermine Hotel sits on top of a closed silver mine. The mine’s tunnels are more than 12 miles (19 km) long and 980 feet (300 m) deep. That’s as deep as the Eiffel Tower is tall! Most of the rooms in the hotel are near the mine’s opening. However, if you want a really special experience, you can spend a night hundreds of feet underground.
pages.brief: In Sala, Sweden, the Sala Silvermine Hotel sits above a closed silver mine with tunnels more than twelve miles long and 980 feet deep. Most rooms are near the mine’s opening, but visitors can choose a special night hundreds of feet underground in the deepest hotel room.

pages.text: The Mine Suite is located more than 500 feet (152 m) beneath the surface. A special guide will lead you down to a room with a bed and chairs, a bathroom, and snacks. Dress in warm clothes. The temperature in the mine itself is only about 28°F (–2°C), but the room is warmed to 64°F (18°C). Wowser! Take a dip in the world’s largest rooftop swimming pool at the Marina Bay Sands Hotel in Singapore. While swimming in a pool that is almost 500 feet (152 m) long, visitors can admire city views from 650 feet (198 m) aboveground!
pages.brief: Deep underground, a guide leads visitors to the Mine Suite more than 500 feet beneath the surface. The warmed room has a bed, chairs, a bathroom, and snacks. Elsewhere, swimmers at Marina Bay Sands Hotel in Singapore enjoy the world’s largest rooftop pool and admire city views from high aboveground.

pages.text: Sleeping with Fish The last stop on your tour is Jules’ Undersea Lodge in Key Largo, Florida. Be prepared to get wet! The lodge is 21 feet (6 m) underwater, resting at the bottom of the Largo Sound lagoon. You’ll need scuba gear to get to your room. The lodge includes two bedrooms and a common room. You can find snacks and breakfast in the common room. For dinner, you can even order pizza. A staff member from the hotel will happily swim it down to you in a watertight box!
pages.brief: In Key Largo, Florida, Jules’ Undersea Lodge rests twenty-one feet underwater at the bottom of a lagoon. Guests use scuba gear to reach the room, which has two bedrooms and a common room. A staff member swims a pizza for dinner down in a watertight box.

pages.text: Conclusion From the forests of Kenya to the bottom of the sea, amazing hotels are everywhere. These incredible places to stay offer you far more than just a bed for the night. They offer you experiences that you’ll never forget! Polar Bear Fun Tundra Lodge in Manitoba, Canada, looks like a train on huge wheels. The entire hotel moves over snow so that guests can get very close to polar bears.
pages.brief: In Manitoba, Canada, the Tundra Lodge looks like a train on huge wheels. The entire hotel moves over snow so guests can get very close to polar bears. Around it, snowy ground and polar bears show an unforgettable wildlife experience.

books.title: Nature Stinks!
books.art_why: Real plants and animals in nature are best shown with photographs.

pages.text: Stinks! Stinks! Some plants and animals rely on their odor as a means of survival. Nature Stinks! is both an informational and an entertaining look at the strange antics of these smelly creatures. Detailed photographs and captions add to the learning.
pages.brief: A photographic introduction to smelly nature shows plants and animals that rely on odor to survive. The scene suggests strange antics of smelly creatures, with a mix of plants and animals grouped together to set up an informational and entertaining look at nature’s stink.

pages.text: Stinky Nature If you’ve ever smelled a skunk, you know it is not a pleasant odor. In fact, it’s terrible! Did you know that both plants and animals can smell bad? Stinky plants usually smell bad to attract insects that help them reproduce. Animals give off odors to attract mates and keep other animals away. Whether plant or animal, nature’s smelliest living things use odors to help them survive.
pages.brief: A skunk releases a terrible odor while nearby stinky plants attract insects and animals use scent to attract mates or keep other animals away. The scene shows both plants and animals using smell to help them survive.

pages.text: Stinky Furry Animals Skunks are probably the most famous smelly animals. They use their odor to keep enemies away. When an enemy gets near, a skunk growls and stomps its feet. If that doesn’t frighten the enemy away, look out! The skunk lifts its tail and sprays a terrible-smelling liquid. The liquid shoots out from the area near the base of its tail. Striped polecats may smell even worse than their skunk cousins. A striped polecat’s spray can cause burning pain.
pages.brief: A skunk growls and stomps its feet at a nearby enemy, then lifts its tail and sprays a terrible-smelling liquid from near the base of its tail. A striped polecat stands nearby, its own spray causing burning pain.

pages.text: Skunks and striped polecats aren’t the only stinky furry animals. The lesser anteater is four times stinkier than a skunk! It, too, shoots a smelly liquid from the area near the base of its tail. Then there’s the opossum. An opossum will pretend to be dead if an enemy is near. This is called “playing possum.” It stays still and releases stinky green slime.
pages.brief: A lesser anteater shoots a smelly liquid from near the base of its tail; it is described as four times stinkier than a skunk. Nearby, an opossum plays dead, staying still while releasing stinky green slime as an enemy is near.

pages.text: A smelly liquid marks the spot where a wolverine has been. A wolverine, or “nasty cat,” also pees on saved food before hiding it. The smell helps the wolverine find the food later and discourages other animals from eating it.
pages.brief: A wolverine, also called a “nasty cat,” marks a spot with smelly liquid and pees on saved food before hiding it. The smell helps the wolverine find the food later and discourages other animals from eating it. The wolverine stands near the marked spot and hidden food.

pages.text: The release of scent can be a warning as well. Male musk oxen fight each other to mate with females. Males use their stinky urine as a signal. It warns other males to keep their distance. The urine sticks to their long belly hair and makes them smell terrible.
pages.brief: Male musk oxen fight each other to mate with females. One male uses stinky urine as a signal that warns other males to keep their distance. The urine sticks to his long belly hair and makes him smell terrible.

pages.text: Stinky Plants The corpse flower is the world’s smelliest flower. This plant smells like rotting flesh. The plant’s disgusting smell attracts flies and beetles that eat rotting animals. These insect visitors don’t find the food they’re looking for, but they pick up pollen. When the insects visit other corpse flowers, they spread the pollen and help corpse flowers reproduce. These flowers also produce their own heat and steam to help their odor spread far and wide. The stinking root parasite doesn’t smell like rotting flesh— it smells like poop! This African plant’s comes from inside its flowers. The smell brings dung beetles, which pollinate it. (Dung is another word for poop. Dung beetles.
pages.brief: The world’s smelliest flower, the corpse flower, releases a rotting-flesh smell, its own heat, and steam, attracting flies and beetles that pick up pollen. Nearby, an African stinking root parasite smells like poop and draws dung beetles that pollinate it.

pages.text: Stinky Birds The hoatzin (wat-SEEN) is the real name for the “stinkbird.” This bird mainly consumes leaves. The food breaks down in the bird’s crop (the area under its throat) before reaching its stomach. This way of eating makes the hoatzin smell awful.
pages.brief: A hoatzin, the real “stinkbird,” mainly eats leaves. The food breaks down in the bird’s crop, the area under its throat, before reaching its stomach. This way of eating makes the hoatzin smell awful. The bird stands among leaves.

pages.text: Vultures are used to bad odors. After all, their diet consists of the stinky flesh of dead animals. When an enemy is near, vultures throw up! The stuff they vomit is extra nasty. It contains rotten meat and stomach acid strong enough to cause burns.
pages.brief: Vultures are used to bad odors because their diet is the stinky flesh of dead animals. When an enemy is near, a vulture throws up extra-nasty stuff containing rotten meat and stomach acid strong enough to cause burns.

pages.text: Stinky Bugs Some bugs also use odor to stay safe. The bombardier beetle can’t fly to escape its enemies, so it has a strong weapon. It can release a hot cloud of stinky, deadly spray. It’s hot enough to kill many enemies and burn humans.
pages.brief: A bombardier beetle cannot fly to escape its enemies, so it releases a hot cloud of stinky, deadly spray. The spray is hot enough to kill many enemies and burn humans. The beetle faces a nearby enemy as the cloud shoots out.

pages.text: What millipedes lack in speed, they make up for in stink. Millipedes can’t move fast, so they need a different way to stay safe. If an enemy comes near, they curl up and give off a stinky liquid. Some millipedes even shoot the smelly stuff.
pages.brief: A millipede cannot move fast, so when an enemy comes near it curls up and gives off a stinky liquid. Some millipedes even shoot the smelly stuff. The scene shows a curled millipede facing a nearby enemy.

pages.text: Other Stinky Animals The common musk turtle has another name—stinkpot! It smells bad when other animals disturb it. A stinky yellow liquid comes out of the back of its body. The mink frog uses scent to keep enemies away as well. Its stink has been compared to rotten onions. It gives off this nasty smell to stay safe from other animals.
pages.brief: A common musk turtle, also called a stinkpot, releases a stinky yellow liquid from the back of its body when disturbed. Nearby, a mink frog gives off a smell compared to rotten onions to keep enemies away.

pages.text: Protecting the Nest The green woodhoopoe lives in Africa south of the Sahara Desert. The female uses odor to protect her nest. She sprays a dark, stinky liquid to keep enemies away. Good and Stinky Being stinky helps many plants and animals stay alive. For plants, the odor brings insects that help them reproduce. For animals, the odor often helps keep enemies away. It can also help an animal eat food or get mates. Stinky steam, spray, vomit, slime, and urine are some of nature’s smelly ways of helping living things survive.
pages.brief: A female green woodhoopoe in Africa south of the Sahara Desert sprays a dark, stinky liquid to protect her nest from enemies. Nearby examples of stinky steam, spray, vomit, slime, and urine suggest nature’s smelly ways of helping living things survive.

books.title: Deep in the Ocean
books.art_why: Real ocean animals, scientists, ships, satellites, and deep-sea equipment exist today and can be photographed.

pages.text: Deep in the Deep in the Deep in the The ocean is a fascinating place for students to explore. Deep in the Ocean describes the plants and animals that can be found in the depths of the ocean and the role of oceanographers in uncovering these creatures’ mysteries.
pages.brief: A wide ocean view opens the book, with bright surface water above and dark depths below; small marine plants and animals suggest the fascinating place students will explore, while the page introduces a book about the deep ocean and the oceanographers who study it.

pages.text: Deep Underwater Imagine taking a trip to the deepest part of the ocean. What kinds of things would you expect to see? Would it be dark or light? Would the water be clear or cloudy? Would it be warm or cold? Would you find strange new animals and plants?
pages.brief: A vast, deep ocean scene invites an imagined trip to the deepest part, showing dark and light areas, clear and cloudy water, and cold regions; strange new animals and plants appear in the depths, prompting wonder about what a traveler would expect to see.

pages.text: Sunlight warms the surface, or shallow parts, of the ocean down to about 200 meters (656 ft). Plants and animals that need sunlight and warm water live there, such as dolphins and sharks. Deep in the ocean, other animals, including squid and viperfish, live in water that is cold and dark.
pages.brief: Sunlight warms the shallow surface water down to about 200 meters, where dolphins and sharks swim among plants and animals that need light and warmth. Below, in cold and dark deep water, a squid and a viperfish live in the ocean depths.

pages.text: Ocean Zones.
pages.brief: A cross-section of the ocean shows different depth zones, from the sunlit shallow surface down through darker middle water to the deep ocean; the zones are arranged one below another to show where ocean life can live at different depths.

pages.text: Diving Deep in the Ocean The deep ocean, below 1,000 meters (3,281 ft), is freezing cold. The weight of water, or water 39.6 meters (130 ft) can harm you. Sport divers wear air tanks filled with a mixture of gases for safety. Deep divers wear a special hard diving suit to protect them from the water pressure. For really deep dives, groups of two or three scientists ride in a small submarine called a submersible.
pages.brief: Deep below 1,000 meters, the ocean is freezing cold and water pressure is dangerous. Sport divers wear air tanks with mixed gases; deep divers wear hard diving suits; groups of two or three scientists ride inside a small submersible for really deep dives.

pages.text: Oceanographers Scientists who study the ocean are called oceanographers (oh-shuh-NOG-ruh-furs). They often live for months on a ship and work seven days a week. Some study what a sea animal eats and where it lives. Others study the ocean water itself. All of them have to understand biology and chemistry. Biology is the study of living things. Chemistry is the study of what things are made of.
pages.brief: Oceanographers work on a ship for months, seven days a week, studying what sea animals eat and where they live, and studying ocean water itself. They need to understand biology, the study of living things, and chemistry, the study of what things are made of.

pages.text: Using Satellites for Tracking Satellites can help to track sea animals’ travels. Scientists tag some animals with electronic sensors. A satellite can track the signal from the tag on the animal’s fin or back. Tracking the signal shows where the animal goes.
pages.brief: A satellite circles above the ocean while a tagged sea animal swims below. Scientists attach electronic sensors to an animal’s fin or back; the satellite tracks the tag’s signal, showing where the animal travels across the sea.

pages.text: Counting the Sea Animals What types of animals live in the ocean? Where do they live? How many are there? Oceanographers studied and counted animals for ten years to learn the answers. They looked at all the world’s oceans from the North Pole to the South Pole. The surprising report is called the Census of Marine Life. Released in 2010, it contains information from more than 540 different groups of researchers.
pages.brief: Oceanographers on ships count sea animals across all the world’s oceans, from the North Pole to the South Pole, during ten years of study. Their surprising report, the Census of Marine Life, released in 2010, contains information from more than 540 groups of researchers.

pages.text: The Census of Marine Life The first surprise was where things lived: everywhere —in all water levels and temperatures! Marine species lived in the hottest and coldest places in the oceans. Some species lived in deep places without light or oxygen. Another surprise was how many new species were discovered. More than twelve hundred new marine species have been described.
pages.brief: The Census of Marine Life revealed marine species living everywhere, in all water levels and temperatures, including the hottest and coldest ocean places and deep spots without light or oxygen. It also showed more than twelve hundred new marine species had been discovered and described.

pages.text: Living in Hot and Cold Water The very cold Deep Ocean Zone has hot volcanoes in it. The water temperature at a volcano can be 400°C (752°F), which is hot enough to melt lead. Some species of shrimp, crabs, worms, and bacteria live in this very hot water. These animals use sulfur to live rather than sunlight.
pages.brief: In the very cold Deep Ocean Zone, hot volcanoes rise from the seafloor. Water at a volcano can reach 400°C, hot enough to melt lead. Shrimp, crabs, worms, and bacteria live in this hot water, using sulfur to live rather than sunlight.

pages.text: Huge groups of Arctic sea life were also found living in freezing water. Some species of squid, cod, and jellyfish live under solid ice that is 700 meters (2,296 ft) thick. Many of these species slow down their movements to save energy so they don’t freeze.
pages.brief: Huge groups of Arctic sea life live in freezing water beneath solid ice 700 meters thick. Squid, cod, and jellyfish are shown under the ice; many slow down their movements to save energy so they do not freeze in the cold water.

pages.text: What Did We Learn? Scientists learned that life is even more adaptable than they had originally thought. Animals living in the deep ocean have found ways to survive in harsh environments. These environments are places where it would be impossible for most other species to survive. The marine census counted more than 230,000 species. More than 6,000 new species had never been seen before! Some creatures were see-through. Some had warning lights that turned on and off. Others had long feelers instead of eyes. Some had teeth so long that they overlapped their jaws. Some made their own antifreeze to stay warm.
pages.brief: A collection of deep-ocean creatures shows how life adapts to harsh places: see-through animals, creatures with warning lights turning on and off, long feelers instead of eyes, teeth so long they overlap the jaws, and animals making their own antifreeze. More than 230,000 species were counted, including over 6,000 never seen before.

pages.text: What else lives in the deep ocean? Scientists keep finding new species and new facts. The more they look, the more they find. They think that only one-fourth of all marine life has been counted. Only some of those species have even been described yet. There are many more surprises to come! Explore More To learn more about the Census of Marine Life, go to its website at www.coml.org. Each week, new discoveries are added to the marine census project map at www.comlmaps.org/ census-on-google-earth. On the Internet, search terms such as deep sea species, blind lobster, or NASA oceanography.
pages.brief: A deep-ocean scene suggests many more surprises to come, with unfamiliar species still waiting to be found. Scientists keep discovering new species and facts; they think only one-fourth of all marine life has been counted, and only some of those species have been described.

books.title: Awesome Ants
books.art_why: Ants are real animals alive today, so photographs fit.

pages.text: In the millions of years that ants have crawled on the earth, they have become some of the most fascinating and amazing insects. Informative and entertaining, Awesome Ants gives students a look into the intricate lives of ants.
pages.brief: A wide outdoor scene shows many ants crawling over grassy ground and a dirt path, with several kinds of ants moving in different directions; the scene suggests the long history and huge numbers of ants on Earth.

pages.text: A Little History You’ve seen them marching through grass and across sidewalks. You may have even seen them crawling over your kitchen counter or inviting themselves to your picnic. They come in colors such as red, yellow, brown, and black. We’re talking about ants—tiny, strong, awesome ants.
pages.brief: Several ants in red, yellow, brown, and black march in a line through green grass and across a gray sidewalk; nearby, a few ants crawl over a kitchen counter and around food on a picnic blanket.

pages.text: Ants are about 100 million years old, which means they were crawling around under the dinosaurs, early mammals, and ancient birds! Between then and now, they’ve changed a lot. Ants used to look more like wasps with shorter jaws. Today, more than 10,000 species of ants live in deserts, rainforests, swamps, and cities. They live on every continent except Antarctica. They have been able to survive so long because of their bodies and how they live. Through the years, they have been able to adapt to changes in their environments.
pages.brief: A prehistoric scene shows ants crawling beneath a dinosaur, early mammals, and ancient birds; in another part, modern ants live in a desert, rainforest, swamp, and city, while a frozen icy land has no ants at all.

pages.text: Body Parts Like all insects, ants have six legs and three body parts. The back part of their body is the abdomen. This part holds the heart and stomachs. Some ants have stingers and poison sacs that they use to protect themselves from predators. Their three pairs of legs attach to the middle part, called the thorax. Each leg has three joints and little hooks that allow ants to climb almost anything. Ants don’t have ears, but they can hear by feeling vibrations through their legs and feet.
pages.brief: A large ant clings to a rough twig, its six jointed legs hooked onto the wood; its three body parts are clearly visible, with a rounded back section and a middle section where the legs attach.

pages.text: The head contains the brain, two eyes, antennae, and jaws. The jaws open and close like scissors. They are used for cutting and carrying things and also for digging and hunting. They are an ant’s most important tool. Ants can lift more than twenty times their own weight. Ants also have other mouthparts for chewing food and drinking.
pages.brief: A close-up of an ant’s head shows two eyes, bending antennae, and scissor-like jaws gripping a crumb; below, the same ant lifts a seed many times its size while other ants dig and carry food with their jaws.

pages.text: The two eyes, called compound eyes, are each made up of many smaller eyes. Even though ants have so many eyes, their eyesight is not very good, so they use their antennae to get around. The antennae are like all-in-one sense machines. Ants use them to taste, smell, hear, and communicate with other ants through touch. The long, thin antennae bend in the middle, like a human’s elbow, and are always moving around. Ants don’t have lungs. Instead they breathe through small holes all over their bodies.
pages.brief: A close-up of an ant’s face shows its two large compound eyes made of many tiny lenses and long antennae bent like elbows; the antennae touch another ant, while tiny openings along the ant’s body suggest how it breathes.

pages.text: Let’s Talk Ants communicate with each other in three ways: touch, sound, and smell. Ants touch each other with their antennae in different ways to send different messages. They can also make noises to communicate by rubbing their legs together or on their bodies. Scientists have learned that these special noises are a call for help.
pages.brief: Two ants stand face to face and touch antennae in a grassy patch; nearby, another ant rubs its legs against its body to make a sound, and a few ants turn toward it as if answering a call for help.

pages.text: The main way ants communicate is by smell. They release special chemicals, called pheromones (FAIR-oh-mohnz), which other ants can smell long after the first ant is gone. Different smells send different messages. For example, a crushed ant releases chemicals that attract other ants. Some chemicals work as an alarm to warn other ants that danger is nearby. The chemicals also make the other ants attack anything near them that is not an ant from the same colony. An ant that has found food will lay down a trail of chemicals for other ants to follow. The trail allows them to find the food and return to the colony. The more ants that follow the trail, the stronger it gets.
pages.brief: A line of ants follows a scent trail across the ground toward a piece of food; one crushed ant lies nearby, and other ants rush toward it, while a few ants turn aggressively toward an ant from another colony.

pages.text: One Big, Happy Family Ant colonies, which can have millions of members, are filled with activity. Some ants are active year-round, while others hibernate in the winter. Some ants build their colonies in logs or trees, but most build their colonies underground. Some ants reinforce the entrance to their colony by mixing twigs into the dirt for added protection from flooding. They have many different rooms, which all have different uses. Some rooms store food or eggs, while others are used to care for the young. Colonies even have rooms for ants to relax in and a special chamber for the queen.
pages.brief: A cutaway view of an underground ant colony shows many chambers connected by tunnels: some rooms hold food and eggs, one room has young ants being cared for, another is for resting, and a special chamber holds the queen; twigs strengthen the entrance above.

pages.text: Within the colony, every ant has a job and special skills to do that job. Worker ants and soldier ants find food and protect the nest. They are social insects and work together as a group. Worker ants are usually the ones you see above the ground. They are the older ants. Other ants build the nest, take care of the young, and do other jobs. The ants that work inside the nest tend to be younger What About the Boys? ants.
